run_count_decision: 3 additional independent runs per configuration (2 -> 5 total), decided and committed in scripts/e2b_stability_rerun_workflow.js BEFORE any new result was seen. C(5,2)=10 pairwise comparisons per configuration, up from C(2,2)=1 -- a 10x increase in sample size.
repetitions: 12 new independent blinded subagent calls (4 configurations x 3 new runs each); 12/12 succeeded, 0 errors, 0 empty results

headline_result.aggregate: 1095/1250 (87.60%), up from 107/125 (85.60%) on the original 2-runs-per-configuration sample -- still below the 90% preregistered bar
headline_result.interpretation: All three real-WANDS-derived configurations independently and consistently sit in an 86-88% band, below 90%, while the smaller synthetic automotive control clears it. A materially more precise (10x larger pairwise sample) measurement pointing at a real, stable population rate for real messy feed data around 86-88%, not a sampling artifact of the original small-N measurement.
headline_result.proposal_vs_validator_instability: 100% of the measured instability is proposal (LLM) instability by construction -- e2b_validator::validate is a pure deterministic function of (proposal, real measured stats); an identical proposal always produces an identical accept/reject decision, so there is no validator-side stochastic contribution to separately measure.
headline_result.accuracy_headline_numbers_unaffected: Baseline 1/2/3 macro F1 (0.5366/0.7985/0.7697), accepted-structural precision/recall, abstention rates, macro F1 by configuration, and end-to-end NDCG/Recall are all byte-identical to the original 2-run measurement -- verified directly, not merely argued -- since build_baselines_2_and_3's headline accepted-descriptor maps use first-run-wins semantics over runs in push order (run 1 always first), which additional runs cannot disturb.
headline_result.go_gate_criterion_4_final: FAIL (87.60% vs >=90% required, on a materially larger and internally consistent sample)

disclosed_limitations: The original 8 passes' own literal prompt wording was never committed to this repository (only their frozen JSON output was) -- the 12 new passes' prompt is a faithful reconstruction from the protocol's own descriptor schema and instructions text, not a byte-identical replay. The bounded INPUT DATA itself (statistics, sample values, shown key names) is, by contrast, fully deterministic and was reproduced exactly.

Model/provider/version for the 12 new passes is whatever this session's configured model serves subagent calls; the original 8 passes' own model/provider/version was likewise never recorded in a machine-readable, pinnable form in this repository, so exact model-identity reproduction could not be verified as matched or mismatched either way.
